options.B: Deep nesting creates overly specific selectors, hard to override and maintain
options.C: SCSS nesting is faster than flat CSS for browser rendering
options.D: Nesting only works 2 levels deep - compiler errors beyond that

quiz.explanation: SCSS nesting: .parent { .child { .grandchild {} } } compiles to .parent .child .grandchild (high specificity). Deep nesting (4+ levels) creates: hard-to-override styles, large CSS output, maintenance issues. Best practice: limit to 3 levels, use BEM methodology, consider if nesting adds value. Nesting is convenient but can become anti-pattern.

quiz.question: What can SCSS variables do that CSS custom properties can't?

options.A: SCSS variables can be changed with JavaScript at runtime
options.B: Used in calculations and functions at compile time, before CSS output
options.C: SCSS variables have better browser support than CSS variables
options.D: CSS custom properties are superior - no advantages for SCSS variables

quiz.explanation: SCSS variables ($color: blue) compile to static values, usable in: color functions (darken($color, 10%)), calculations, conditionals (@if), loops. CSS custom properties work at runtime, changeable with JS. SCSS variables compile away (no runtime cost). Use both: SCSS for compile-time logic, CSS vars for runtime theming.

quiz.question: When should you use @extend instead of mixins?

options.A: @extend is always better - more performant than mixins
options.B: @extend for shared selectors without params; mixins for parameterized reuse
options.C: Mixins are deprecated - modern SCSS only uses @extend
options.D: They're identical - @extend is just shorter mixin syntax

quiz.explanation: @extend shares selectors: .error { color: red; } .serious-error { @extend .error; } outputs .error, .serious-error { color: red }. Mixins duplicate code at each @include. Use @extend for: simple shared styles, no parameters. Use mixins for: parameters, @content, complex logic. Warning: @extend can create unexpected selector chains, many prefer mixins or utility classes.

quiz.question: What's the benefit of media query mixins in SCSS?

options.A: Media queries don't work in regular CSS - require SCSS
options.B: Centralize breakpoints, avoid hardcoding values throughout codebase
options.C: SCSS media queries are faster than CSS media queries
options.D: Mixins automatically generate all responsive breakpoints

quiz.explanation: Define breakpoint mixin: @mixin tablet { @media (min-width: 768px) { @content; } }. Use: .box { width: 100%; @include tablet { width: 50%; } }. Benefits: centralized breakpoint values, easy updates, consistent naming. Can use variables: @mixin above($bp) { @media (min-width: $bp) { @content; } }. DRY principle for responsive design.

quiz.question: How do SCSS functions differ from mixins?

options.A: Functions return values for use in properties; mixins output CSS blocks
options.B: Functions are deprecated - only use mixins in modern SCSS
options.C: Mixins are faster - functions add compilation overhead
options.D: They're identical - functions just use different syntax

quiz.explanation: Functions return values: @function double($n) { @return $n * 2; }. Use: width: double(10px). Mixins output CSS: @mixin center { display: flex; justify-content: center; }. Functions for: calculations, color manipulation (lighten, darken), string operations. Mixins for: reusable style blocks. Can't use functions where CSS blocks expected.

quiz.question: Why is @use recommended over @import in modern SCSS?

options.A: @import is faster and has better browser compatibility
options.B: @use creates namespaces, avoids global pollution, clearer dependencies
options.C: @use is deprecated - Sass team recommends @import only
options.D: They're identical - @use is just newer syntax for same behavior

quiz.explanation: @import: loads globally, no namespacing, can cause conflicts, deprecated. @use: creates namespace, explicit dependencies, loads once. Example: @use 'colors' as c; background: c.$primary. Benefits: no naming conflicts, clear where variables/mixins come from, better performance (load once). @import removed in Dart Sass 3.0 - migrate to @use/@forward.

quiz.question: What is the purpose of generateStaticParams in Next.js App Router?

options.B: Pre-render dynamic routes at build time
options.C: Fetch data on the client side

quiz.explanation: generateStaticParams is used to define a list of route segment parameters that should be statically generated at build time. It replaces getStaticPaths from Pages Router and enables static generation of dynamic routes like /products/[id].
quiz.whyImportant: You used this in your project for category/[slug] and products/[productId]

quiz.question: How does Next.js Image component optimize images?

options.B: Lazy loading, format optimization, responsive sizing
options.C: Converts all images to WebP only

quiz.explanation: Next.js Image component provides automatic lazy loading, serves modern formats (WebP, AVIF) to supporting browsers, generates responsive sizes based on device, and optimizes on-demand rather than at build time. It significantly improves LCP and reduces bandwidth usage.
quiz.whyImportant: You used this extensively in ProductCard and Product components

quiz.question: What does the 'sizes' prop in Next.js Image component do?

options.B: Tells browser which image size to load for different viewports

quiz.explanation: The sizes prop is a media query string that tells the browser which image size to request based on viewport width. For example: '(max-width: 768px) 100vw, 400px' means use full viewport width on mobile, 400px on larger screens. This enables responsive images and reduces bandwidth on mobile.
quiz.whyImportant: You used sizes='(max-width: 768px) 100vw, 400px' in your ProductCard

quiz.question: How do you properly persist cart data using localStorage in React?

options.A: useEffect with empty deps to save on mount
options.B: useEffect with state deps to save on changes

quiz.explanation: Use useEffect with state dependencies to save to localStorage whenever state changes, and use lazy initialization in useState to load initial state from localStorage. This pattern ensures data persists across sessions while avoiding unnecessary writes and race conditions.
quiz.whyImportant: This is exactly how your CartContext works

quiz.question: Why use JSON.parse with try-catch when loading from localStorage?

options.B: Corrupted data could break JSON.parse

quiz.explanation: localStorage stores only strings, so JSON.parse is needed to convert back to objects. However, if data is corrupted, manually edited, or from an old app version, JSON.parse will throw. Using try-catch with fallback to initial value prevents app crashes and handles edge cases gracefully.
quiz.whyImportant: You implemented this exact pattern in CartContext initialization

quiz.question: What are CSS Modules and how do they prevent style conflicts?

options.B: Automatically scoped classes via unique hashing

quiz.explanation: CSS Modules automatically scope CSS by generating unique class names (e.g., .button becomes .Button_button__abc123). This prevents style conflicts between components, enables local reasoning about styles, and works with standard CSS/SCSS syntax. It's the default in Next.js.
quiz.whyImportant: Your entire project uses SCSS Modules (*.module.scss)

quiz.question: Why use @use instead of @import in modern Sass?

options.A: @import is deprecated and will be removed
options.B: @use is faster

quiz.explanation: @import is deprecated and will be removed in Dart Sass 3.0. @use provides better namespace management, avoids duplicate CSS output, and makes dependencies explicit. It's the modern way to load Sass modules and is required for using Sass built-in modules like sass:color.
quiz.whyImportant: You migrated from darken() to @use 'sass:color' in your project

quiz.question: What is the modern alternative to Sass darken() function?

options.B: color.adjust() with negative lightness

quiz.explanation: darken() is deprecated. Use color.adjust($color, $lightness: -10%) instead. This is part of the sass:color module and provides more consistent color manipulation. You must @use 'sass:color' first to access these functions.
quiz.whyImportant: You literally fixed this in your project! Changed darken() to darken-color() using color.adjust()

quiz.question: How do you test localStorage in Jest/React Testing Library?
